medical_history.chief_complaint: Chronic abdominal pain and bowel irregularity

social_history.diet: Previously high-processed foods, now attempting low-FODMAP
social_history.stress_level: High - work stress, parenting two young children

visits.chief_complaint: 3-month history of abdominal cramping, alternating diarrhea and constipation, bloating
visits.hpi: 37 yo F presents with 3-month history of diffuse abdominal pain, cramping in nature, severity 5-7/10, worse with stress and certain foods. Reports alternating loose stools (Bristol 6-7) and constipation (Bristol 1-2). Episodes occur 3-4x/week. Associated bloating, worse after meals. Denies blood in stool, weight loss, fever, nocturnal symptoms. Symptoms began around time of increased work stress (new curriculum implementation). Pain partially relieved by bowel movements.

physical_exam.general: Alert, well-appearing, in no acute distress
physical_exam.abdomen: Soft, non-distended, mild diffuse tenderness without rebound or guarding. Normal bowel sounds. No masses or organomegaly.
physical_exam.rectal: Deferred - will consider if alarm symptoms develop

assessment_plan.diagnosis: Suspected IBS - Mixed Type (Rome IV criteria met)
orders: Stool culture and O&P if diarrhea persists
medications: Psyllium fiber 1 tablespoon daily with 8oz water
education: Discussed Rome IV criteria for IBS diagnosis
Food diary - track symptoms and triggers
Red flag symptoms to report immediately
assessment_plan.follow_up: 2 weeks - review lab results, assess symptom improvement

visits.subjective: Pt returns for lab review. Reports partial improvement with hyoscyamine - helps with acute cramping episodes. Fiber causing increased bloating. Food diary shows possible triggers: dairy, onions, beans, apples. Stress level remains high.

assessment_plan.diagnosis: IBS-M (IBS Mixed Type) - K58.2 - labs support functional diagnosis, no evidence of IBD or celiac
plan: D/C psyllium - switch to smooth texture Metamucil or Benefiber
Start low-FODMAP diet - provided handouts and app recommendation
Referred to GI nutritionist (Sarah Thompson, RD)
Start Vitamin D3 2000 IU daily
Continue hyoscyamine PRN
Consider trial of probiotic (VSL#3 or Culturelle)
assessment_plan.counseling: Explained IBS pathophysiology, visceral hypersensitivity, gut-brain axis. Discussed importance of stress management. Recommended cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) or gut-directed hypnotherapy resources.
assessment_plan.follow_up: 6 weeks - assess response to dietary modifications

visits.subjective: Pt reports 40-50% improvement with low-FODMAP elimination phase. Met with nutritionist 2x. Identified major triggers: wheat, garlic, onions, dairy. Diarrhea episodes decreased from 3-4x/week to 1-2x/week. Constipation remains problematic - going 4-5 days between BMs. Cramping less severe (3-4/10). Bloating improved. Still not meeting with therapist due to time constraints/work schedule.

assessment_plan.diagnosis: IBS-M, responding to dietary management but constipation-predominant currently
plan: Continue low-FODMAP diet with reintroduction phase guidance
Start polyethylene glycol 3350 (MiraLAX) 17g daily for constipation
Continue probiotic and vitamin D
Hyoscyamine PRN (using 2-3x/week - good)
Strongly encourage stress management - provided list of therapists specializing in CBT for GI disorders
Consider pelvic floor PT if constipation doesn't improve

visits.subjective: Pt doing much better overall. MiraLAX helpful - now BM every 2-3 days, softer consistency (Bristol 4-5). Completed FODMAP reintroduction - tolerates small amounts of lactose-free dairy, avoids wheat/garlic/onions/beans. Diarrhea rare (maybe 1x/month). Cramping minimal. Started therapy 1 month ago - finding it helpful for stress management. Lost 3 lbs unintentionally but feels healthy. Energy better. Some concern about social limitations with diet.

plan: Continue current management - MiraLAX, low-FODMAP with modifications
Continue therapy - excellent progress
Discussed flexible approach to diet - 80/20 rule for social situations
May try reducing MiraLAX to every other day to find minimum effective dose
Continue probiotic
Repeat Vitamin D level in 3 months
assessment_plan.education: Reinforced that IBS is chronic, waxing/waning condition. Expect flares with stress/illness. Discussed long-term management strategies.

visits.subjective: Pt calls with 2-week history of worsening symptoms. Increased diarrhea (5-6x/day, Bristol 7), severe cramping (7-8/10), urgency. No blood, fever, or weight loss. Denies recent travel or sick contacts. Reports high stress - mother hospitalized with Crohn's flare. Dietary adherence poor past 2 weeks due to stress/eating on-the-go. Stopped MiraLAX when diarrhea started.

plan: Stop MiraLAX until diarrhea resolves
Start loperamide 2mg after loose stool (max 8mg/day)
Return to strict low-FODMAP diet
Increase hyoscyamine use PRN for cramping
Consider short course dicyclomine 20mg TID if cramping not controlled
Hydration crucial - electrolyte drinks
If no improvement in 1 week or develops alarm symptoms → stool studies to r/o infection
medications_added: Loperamide 2mg PRN after loose stool (max 4 doses/day)

visits.subjective: Phone follow-up. Pt reports improvement. Diarrhea decreased to 2-3x/day. Cramping better with dicyclomine (now 4-5/10). Back on low-FODMAP diet. Mother discharged from hospital - stress level improving. Using loperamide 1-2x/day.

plan: Continue current regimen
Taper dicyclomine over next week (TID → BID → daily → stop)
Continue loperamide PRN for next few days then reassess need
Resume MiraLAX at low dose (8.5g daily) once diarrhea fully resolved
Encouraged to maintain therapy appointments through stressful period

visits.subjective: Pt back to baseline. Bowel movements every 2-3 days, Bristol 4. Minimal cramping. Back on MiraLAX 17g every other day. Diet adherence good. Therapy ongoing. Mother recovering well. Pt asking about medication alternatives - concerned about long-term MiraLAX use and wants something more 'natural'.

plan: Reassured about MiraLAX safety for long-term use
Discussed alternative: magnesium citrate 200-400mg nightly (natural option)
Trial switch from MiraLAX to magnesium citrate 200mg nightly
Continue low-FODMAP diet modifications
Continue probiotic
Vitamin D - continue 2000 IU daily (recheck in 6 months)

visits.subjective: Pt doing well. Magnesium works as well as MiraLAX - BM every 2 days, soft formed. No diarrhea episodes since February flare. Cramping rare. Diet liberalized somewhat but still avoids major triggers. Therapy completed - using stress management techniques independently. Energy good. No new concerns. Here for routine check-in.

plan: Continue current regimen - working well
No medication changes
Discussed importance of maintaining stress management, diet awareness
Reinforced to call with any concerning symptoms (blood, weight loss, nocturnal symptoms, fever)
Discussed colonoscopy screening - due at age 45 (2032) but given family history of colon cancer, consider starting at age 40 (2027)

visits.subjective: 6-month routine check-in. Pt continues to do very well. BM every 2 days, Bristol 4. Minimal cramping or bloating. Managing diet well. Work stress moderate but managing well with previous CBT techniques. Minor 3-day flare in November (cramping/loose stools) related to stomach virus - resolved on its own. Otherwise stable.

plan: Continue current successful regimen: magnesium citrate 200mg nightly, low-FODMAP diet awareness, probiotic
Discussed option to trial reducing magnesium dose to find minimum effective dose
Continue vitamin D 2000 IU daily
No medication changes at this time
Reinforced sustainable lifestyle modifications
assessment_plan.follow_up: 6 months or PRN for any flares

visits.subjective: Annual wellness check-in. Pt continues to do very well. BM every 2 days, Bristol 4, no pain. No flares in past 6 months. Diet comfortable and sustainable - has found good balance with social situations. Work-life balance good. Children doing well (now ages 12 and 9). Asking about reducing medications since feeling so stable.

assessment_plan.diagnosis: IBS-M - excellent long-term control (2+ years stability)
plan: Discussed option to trial stopping magnesium to see if still needed - pt prefers to continue given excellent control with minimal medication burden
Continue current successful regimen
No medication changes
Continue vitamin D 2000 IU daily
Continue probiotic
Updated colonoscopy screening plan - schedule at age 40 (2027) given father's colon cancer history
Continue monitoring annually
assessment_plan.education: Congratulated patient on excellent symptom management. Reinforced sustainable lifestyle modifications. Discussed that IBS is chronic condition but with proper management can be minimally impactful on quality of life.
assessment_plan.follow_up: Annual visit 2025, or sooner PRN for any flares or new symptoms

quality_of_life_assessment.work_impact: Minimal - no missed work days in past year

clinical_pearls: Patient's IBS strongly correlated with stress/anxiety - gut-brain axis evident
Low-FODMAP diet was transformative - identified wheat, garlic, onions, beans as major triggers
Required multi-modal approach: dietary modification, stress management (CBT), appropriate pharmacotherapy
Family history significant for GI disease (mother: Crohn's, father: colon CA, brother: celiac) - increased surveillance appropriate
Excellent example of successful long-term IBS management with minimal medication burden
Stress-triggered flare (mother's hospitalization) demonstrated importance of gut-brain connection
Patient achieved excellent quality of life with combination of lifestyle modifications and targeted medications
notes.red_flags_monitored: No alarm symptoms present throughout care - no blood in stool, no unintentional weight loss, no nocturnal symptoms, no fever. These would warrant imaging/endoscopy.
notes.patient_engagement: Highly engaged patient, excellent adherence to dietary modifications, completed CBT therapy, maintains food diary, proactive about symptom management
